name: Chewing towel method

card.summary: The towel method is a do-it-yourself jaw exercise in which a folded towel is bitten and chewed to train the masseter muscles, with the aim of a more defined, squarer jawline.
card.note: Dental professionals cited in coverage warn about jaw joint strain, tooth stress and unwanted masseter bulk.

quick.overview:
The towel method uses a thick folded towel as chewing resistance, as a free alternative to gum or commercial jaw trainers. The idea is that working the masseter, the main chewing muscle at the angle of the jaw, makes it larger and gives a more sculpted lower face.

It spread through TikTok and Instagram in the early 2020s and is discussed in looksmaxxing and mewing circles. No clinical trial has tested the towel method itself, though the masseter is known to enlarge with habitual clenching or heavy chewing.
quick.how: Practitioners describe folding a hand towel several times into a thick stack, biting it and performing chewing movements or clenching holds for short sessions repeated over weeks. Some pair it with posture or mewing routines.
quick.risks: Dentists and jaw specialists quoted in coverage of jaw-training devices caution about temporomandibular joint (TMJ) pain, headaches and tooth wear or movement from repeated hard biting. Masseter growth can also make the lower face wider or asymmetric rather than more refined.

lead: The chewing towel method, usually called the towel method, is a social-media jaw exercise in which a folded towel is bitten and chewed or clenched on to work the masseter muscles. It is promoted as a no-cost alternative to jaw-training devices and gum, with the aim of a more defined jawline and less visible lower-face softness. [1]

It emerged on TikTok and Instagram in the early 2020s and circulated in looksmaxxing and mewing communities. One TikTok video by @plainjad claiming results within a week is reported to have passed 7.5 million views. [1] A looksmax.org thread argues, from the opposing side, that chewing gum will not produce masseter hypertrophy and that the muscle should be trained like any other with heavy, low-rep resistance, so a towel can be treated as a way to add load. [2]

Anatomically, the masseter is a thick chewing muscle that can enlarge with habitual teeth clenching, grinding (bruxism) or constant gum chewing; the enlargement is usually painless and appears at the angle of the jaw. [3] No published trial has studied the towel method itself.

chain: Bite and chew a folded towel against resistance
Masseter works harder and may grow
Wider, more defined lower face and jaw angle
angle.text: Proponents say that resistance chewing builds the masseter the way weights build other muscles, giving the lower face more width and definition. The mechanism of masseter enlargement from heavy chewing is recognised, but results from the towel method have not been measured.

paras: In the standard description, a hand towel is folded four to six times into a thick stack, or two to three times if it is very thick or the mouth is small, then bitten firmly with chewing motions or clenching holds. It is said to work the masseter mainly, with some engagement of neck and chin muscles. [1]

The method became visible as a viral short-form video trend in the early 2020s under hashtags such as #JawlineTok, with creators posting tutorials and before-and-after claims, and it spread into looksmaxxing, mewing and male-aesthetics forums as an equipment-free option. [1]

On looksmax.org it appears in arguments about whether gum chewing 'works': one poster contends that chewing gum is insufficient for hypertrophy and that masseters need high-intensity, low-repetition training. [2]

The masseter raises the jaw and has superficial, deep and coronoid parts. It can enlarge from clenching, grinding or constant gum chewing; the enlargement is usually soft and painless, typically on both sides, and patients often seek assessment because of how the face looks. The enlargement may be uneven, so asymmetry can occur. [3]

Coverage describing the trend lists potential risks including TMJ disorders, jaw pain, headaches, tooth misalignment or damage from repeated hard biting, and unwanted masseter bulk that squares the jaw. Dental professionals are reported to caution against unverified resistance-based jaw exercises. [1]
No studies found. Related research concerns masseter enlargement from habitual clenching and chewing, as described in anatomical references. [3]

timeline.event: The towel method spreads on TikTok and Instagram as a jaw-training alternative. [1]

lore.intro: In looksmaxxing forums, the towel method is discussed alongside gum chewing and jaw-trainer devices as a way to add masseter size. [1][2]

claims.claim: Chewing a folded towel builds the masseters and sharpens the jawline
claims.believers: Proponents and viral creators say visible results appear within weeks and that it is a free substitute for devices. [1]
claims.experts: No published studies have tested the towel method; the masseter is known to enlarge with habitual clenching or heavy chewing. [3]

claims.claim: Gum is too weak to grow the masseter, so heavier resistance is needed
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster says masseters respond like other muscles to high intensity and low reps. [2]
claims.experts: Anatomical sources note that constant gum chewing can enlarge the masseter. [3]

claims.claim: Hard biting for a jawline can cause joint and dental problems
claims.believers: Critics in coverage of the trend cite TMJ pain, headaches and tooth stress. [1]
claims.experts: Dental professionals are reported to caution against resistance-based jaw exercises without verification. [1]
